Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
444 AM EDT Tue Mar 24 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The Small Craft Advisory on the ocean will now expire at Noon
(16Z) today.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) High pressure will largely be control through Thursday along
with gradually warming temperatures.  

2) Rain is likely Thursday night followed by cold and dry 
conditions for the upcoming weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
A fast, nearly zonal flow will feature broadscale ridging across
the western half of the country, and weak troughing across the 
east. Surface high pressure will largely be in control during 
this time with a series of weak disturbances passing to the 
north. There is a low chance of some warm advection showers 
Thursday afternoon as high pressure moves offshore. In addition,
there is abundant mid and high level moisture riding overtop 
the western ridge, which is expected to spill into the area 
tonight into Wednesday. Expect mostly cloud conditions during 
this time.

Temperatures look to be a few degrees below normal today, but 
then warm into Thursday. Highs by Thursday are forecast to be in
the 50s for much of the CT coast and eastern LI, but as you work
to the NW and away from marine influence, expect highs in the
60s to possibly 70. The latter of which will likely be dependent
on the extent of the cloud cover.


.KEY MESSAGE 2... 
A cold front is progged to move across the region Thursday night 
into early Friday. The best chance for rain at this time looks
to be after midnight. This is when the modeling is coming into 
agreement with the most organized lift/convergence coinciding 
with moisture. The atmosphere quickly dries out Friday morning 
behind the cold front. Temperatures should be able to rise well 
into the 50s across the area as dew points drop throughout the 
day. Dry conditions will continue into next Monday with high 
pressure in control. Daytime temperatures will likely end up 
well below normal on Saturday in the low to mid 40s, before 
slowly trending milder Sunday into next Monday. High 
temperatures by next Monday should be in the 50s. The coldest 
nights appear to be Friday and Saturday night with temperatures 
in the 20s and lower 30s, coldest inland.

&&

.AVIATION /08Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
High pressure over the terminals today.

VFR conditions expected through the TAF period. 

NW winds 8-12kt become light and variable for a few hours this 
afternoon as a weak surface trough develops. Winds then become 
light S/SW late in the afternoon.

    NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty... 

Wind shift to S/SW may be off +/- 1-2 hours.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY... 

Wednesday night: VFR.

Thursday: VFR with a slight chance of rain in the evening, MVFR or 
lower late at night with rain likely. SW wind gusts 15-20 kt.

Friday: Chance of rain early with MVFR or lower possible. NW wind 
gusts 15-20 kt.

Saturday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions on the ocean ware expect to come to an end by 
noon (16Z) as winds and seas fall off as high pressure works in
from the west. SCA conditions are likely on the ocean Thursday 
in a southerly flow and could potentially expand to the non- 
ocean waters due to a cold front passage on Friday. SCA 
conditions may then linger into Friday on the ocean. Winds and 
seas subside Friday night into Saturday as high pressure builds 
towards the waters.

&&
